report.verdict: We checked this artifact against 51 deterministic rules from corpus-2026.09 and 10 matched, on 100% coverage. That places it in the "many known signals" band at 72 of 99. Every match below cites what we read and where.

DOM nodes walked

script responses captured. Zero means the response filter went stale and the source-map, bundle-weight and vendor-host rules all passed having scanned nothing. This is the exact bug the source corpus shipped for months.
well-known paths probed
words of rendered innerText. Zero means the page rendered nothing readable.

elements whose computed animation and transition values were read, then re-read under an emulated prefers-reduced-motion. Zero means the motion walk went stale and every uniformity rule below it passed having measured nothing.

images text recovery was ATTEMPTED on. This counts attempts, not successes: an image nothing could be read from is stored with the reason, because an unread image is not an image with no words in it. Zero is legitimate here, and only here, because a page can honestly have no images.

lines.title: The page names an AI site builder in its generator tag

evidence.expected: absent, or your own build identifier

lines.explanation: A <meta name="generator"> naming an AI site builder is the builder saying so itself. This is the single most direct piece of evidence in the corpus and it is readable in view-source.
lines.falsePositiveNote: A tag is a claim about the TOOL, not about the effort. A designer can build something careful in one of these and leave the tag in. It also says nothing about who wrote the copy.
lines.prevention: If the build is yours, own the output: remove the vendor generator tag or replace it with your own build identifier.

remediation.sourceHint: the head of the root layout or the template that renders <head>
remediation.summary: Remove the vendor generator meta tag, or replace it with the build identifier for this project.
remediation.doNotApplyIf: the tag is wanted for tooling that reads it, in which case set it to something that names this build rather than the vendor.
remediation.rebuttal: A tag is a claim about the TOOL, not about the effort. A designer can build something careful in one of these and leave the tag in. It also says nothing about who wrote the copy.

lines.title: The site is served from a bare hosting-platform subdomain
lines.explanation: A production site on a raw *.vercel.app / *.lovable.app / *.repl.co host has skipped the one step that costs money and takes a human decision: a domain.
lines.falsePositiveNote: Staging URLs, internal tools, demos and hobby projects live here legitimately, and none of that is a defect. What it is not is a shipped product.
lines.prevention: Put it on a domain you own and make the platform URL redirect or noindex.

remediation.summary: Serve this from a domain the operator owns, and let the platform URL redirect to it.
remediation.guidance: A domain is a purchase and a DNS change, not an edit, so nothing is proposed here. If the platform URL has to stay reachable, redirect it or mark it noindex so it is not the canonical version.
remediation.doNotApplyIf: this is a staging URL, an internal tool, a demo or a hobby project, none of which needs a domain.
remediation.rebuttal: Staging URLs, internal tools, demos and hobby projects live here legitimately, and none of that is a defect. What it is not is a shipped product.

lines.title: The real headline face is one of the AI-default sans set

evidence.expected: a face chosen for this project

lines.explanation: Inter, Geist or Space Grotesk as the actual rendered headline face. Free, excellent, and the default output of every generator, which is exactly why it reads as one.
lines.falsePositiveNote: Inter is a genuinely great typeface used deliberately by serious teams. This is the weakest kind of evidence in the corpus and it is weighted accordingly.
lines.prevention: Any other competent face moves the read. It does not have to be expensive: none of the four funded comparables measured used Inter as their real face.

remediation.summary: Choose a headline face for this project rather than the default (GeistSans).
remediation.guidance: Any other competent face moves the read, and it does not have to be an expensive one. Which face is a brand decision, so none is proposed.
remediation.doNotApplyIf: this face was chosen deliberately, which is a perfectly reasonable thing to have done.
remediation.rebuttal: Inter is a genuinely great typeface used deliberately by serious teams. This is the weakest kind of evidence in the corpus and it is weighted accordingly.

lines.title: One typeface for the entire page

evidence.locator: font-family across h1, body and UI
evidence.expected: at least two voices, or a real optical axis

lines.explanation: A single computed font-family across headings, body and UI. Every premium reference page in the calibration set has two voices; a monoculture is what you get when nobody chose.
lines.falsePositiveNote: One-face systems are a legitimate and sometimes excellent decision, particularly with a variable face carrying real optical range.
lines.prevention: Add one second voice for display, or use a real optical-size axis so the headline is not just the body text made large.

remediation.locator: font-family across h1, body and UI
remediation.summary: Add a second voice for display, or use a face with a real optical-size axis.
remediation.guidance: Which second face is a brand decision, so none is proposed. The observation is that headings, body and UI all compute to one family.
remediation.doNotApplyIf: the one-face system is deliberate and the face carries real optical range.
addresses: font-family across h1, body and UI
remediation.rebuttal: One-face systems are a legitimate and sometimes excellent decision, particularly with a variable face carrying real optical range.

lines.title: robots.txt or sitemap.xml missing, or unreferenced
lines.explanation: No robots.txt, no sitemap.xml, or a sitemap that robots.txt never points at. A sitemap nothing references is a sitemap nothing finds.
lines.falsePositiveNote: Small sites are crawled fine without either. This is a completeness signal, not a functional problem.
lines.prevention: Serve both, and reference the sitemap from robots.txt.

remediation.summary: Serve /robots.txt, and reference the sitemap from robots.txt.
remediation.guidance: Both files are served by the app or the host rather than declared in the document that was rendered, so this is named rather than patched.
remediation.doNotApplyIf: the site is small and crawled fine without either, which is common.
remediation.rebuttal: Small sites are crawled fine without either. This is a completeness signal, not a functional problem.

lines.title: No link preview image
lines.explanation: No og:image, so every share of this link renders as a grey box in every chat app it is pasted into.
lines.falsePositiveNote: Irrelevant for a site nobody shares, such as an internal tool.

remediation.guidance: An image generated from the page title beats nothing, but which image is a design decision and the file does not exist yet, so no value is proposed.

lines.title: No canonical URL
lines.explanation: Without a canonical, every ?ref= and ?utm_ variant of this URL is indexed as a separate duplicate page.
lines.falsePositiveNote: Only matters for pages that are shared with tracking parameters attached.
lines.prevention: Emit a canonical link on every indexable page.

remediation.sourceHint: the head of the layout or the page metadata for this route
remediation.summary: Add a canonical link pointing at https://v0-flappy-bird-game-lilac.vercel.app/, which is the URL this read resolved to.
remediation.doNotApplyIf: this page is a variant that should canonicalise to a different URL, or the final URL carries tracking parameters that should not be the canonical form.
remediation.rebuttal: Only matters for pages that are shared with tracking parameters attached.

lines.title: No favicon
lines.explanation: No icon is reachable and none is declared, so the tab shows a blank sheet.
lines.falsePositiveNote: Cosmetic. Included because it is the cheapest possible sign that nobody looked at the tab.
lines.prevention: Ship an icon.

remediation.summary: Ship an icon and declare it.
remediation.guidance: The file does not exist yet, so there is nothing to patch. This is the cheapest item in the corpus and the most visible in a tab strip.
remediation.doNotApplyIf: nothing, beyond not caring how the tab looks.
remediation.rebuttal: Cosmetic. Included because it is the cheapest possible sign that nobody looked at the tab.

lines.title: The framework's out-of-the-box transition, everywhere

evidence.locator: dominant transition timing across the page
evidence.observed: 11 of 12 transitions (92%) compute to 150ms cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 0.2, 1), which is the framework default
evidence.expected: a duration and easing chosen for this page

lines.explanation: Eight or more elements with a transition, and 60% or more of them compute to EXACTLY Tailwind's shipped default pairing: 150ms with cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 0.2, 1). Not a uniform value, a specific one: the number nobody chose. Four generated pages read in August 2026 (three v0, one Lovable) all land on it, and the five hand-built pages in the negative corpus compute 300ms ease-in-out, 300ms ease, 200ms ease and 200ms cubic-bezier(0.44, 0, 0.56, 1) instead, because somebody typed those.
lines.falsePositiveNote: This is a DEFAULT, not a fingerprint. A hand-built Tailwind site whose author never touched the motion config computes the same values honestly, and there are a great many of those. It is a visual-default-flavoured tell wearing a motion coat, which is why it is weighted below the uniformity rule and why the family is capped at 12%.
lines.prevention: Set a duration and an easing you chose. Two lines in the theme, and the page stops sharing its timing with every other Tailwind page on the internet.

remediation.locator: dominant transition timing across the page
remediation.summary: Choose a duration and an easing, in the theme, once.
remediation.guidance: No values are proposed: which pace suits the page is the author's call, and the finding is that nobody has made it yet rather than that 150ms is wrong. Anything set deliberately clears this rule, including 150ms set deliberately, which the measurement cannot distinguish and which is why the weight is small.
remediation.doNotApplyIf: the framework default was chosen after consideration, in which case the honest answer is that this rule cannot see the difference.
addresses: dominant transition timing across the page
remediation.rebuttal: This is a DEFAULT, not a fingerprint. A hand-built Tailwind site whose author never touched the motion config computes the same values honestly, and there are a great many of those. It is a visual-default-flavoured tell wearing a motion coat, which is why it is weighted below the uniformity rule and why the family is capped at 12%.

evidence.expected: n/a: this argues FOR the artifact
n/a: this argues FOR the artifact

lines.explanation: A CSSFontFaceRule serving a face that is not on the known-free list, from this origin. Somebody chose a typeface, paid for it, and self-hosted the files. Generators do not license type.
lines.falsePositiveNote: A face can be absent from the free list because it is obscure rather than because it is paid for, and a trial or DEMO build is licence sloppiness rather than investment. Read the src, it is printed.

families.title: Builder fingerprints
families.caveat: The strongest signals here are also the easiest to delete. A vendor can strip a generator tag in one release, so this family is capped and the score has to stand up without it.

families.title: Default visual language
families.caveat: Highest false-positive risk in the corpus. Skilled human designers converge on the same defaults, so no single visual tell counts for much and several are suppressed when they stand alone.

families.title: Craft floor
families.caveat: This family measures ABSENT CRAFT, not generation. A rushed human trips every check in it. Weighted lowest on purpose.

families.title: Motion signature
families.caveat: Motion SAMENESS is the signal, not motion. Funded human sites animate too, often better, so nothing here fires on the presence of an animation: every rule needs a distribution (one duration and one easing across most of the page, delay deltas that are exactly equal, an infinite loop on decoration). Capped above structural uniformity because a stagger ladder is configured rather than defaulted, and well below a builder fingerprint because a design system produces uniform motion honestly.
